description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Reference Variables and Assignment".

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a reference parameter in a method signature?
questions.explanation: The 'ref' keyword is used in C# to pass an argument by reference, meaning any change to the parameter in the method will be reflected in the original variable.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Since 'a' is passed by reference using 'ref', the operation 'a = 5 * 5' modifies the original variable 'a' in the Main method. Output: 25.

questions.question: Select the WRONG statement about the 'ref' keyword in C#:

options.text: The 'ref' keyword causes arguments to be passed by reference
Changes made using 'ref' parameters are reflected in the original variable
Variables passed as 'ref' must be initialized before they are passed

questions.explanation: Statement 'a' is incorrect because 'ref' is simply a parameter modifier; it has nothing to do with recursion unless a method calls itself using those parameters.

questions.question: Select the correct difference between '=' and '==' in C#.

options.text: '==' is for assignment, '=' is for comparison
'=' is for assignment, '==' is for comparison

questions.explanation: The '=' operator assigns the value on the right to the variable on the left. The '==' operator compares the equality of two values.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Assignment operators are evaluated right-to-left. 1) b /= (4 * 2) -> b = 2 / 8 = 0. 2) x -= 0 -> x = 4 - 0 = 4. Result: 4 0.

questions.question:
What is the result of the following C# expression if a is int, b is float, and c is long?

a += (float) b /= (long) c;
questions.explanation: (float) b is a value, not a variable, so it cannot be the left-hand side of /=. The expression does not compile (CS0131).
